CanBeGeneratedByModifiers.rationale: `=> false` (CurseOfTheBell.cs:8) == the class attribute; the curse comes with Calling Bell, not from the random-curse pool, on both sides.

CanonicalKeywords.rationale: `{ Eternal, Unplayable }` (CurseOfTheBell.cs:12-16) == both flags. NOT Ethereal, and the sim correctly leaves `is_ethereal` False.

ctor.issue: CURSE / CURSE / NONE map exactly. The canonical energy cost is -1 in C# and 0 in the sim. `CardEnergyCost.GetWithModifiers` returns early on `_base < 0` (CardEnergyCost.cs:100-103), so the game's unplayable card is immune to every local and global cost modifier and keeps reporting -1; the sim runs a base of 0 through the full modifier chain in `Card.energy_cost` (cards/base.py:222-232). `GetAmountToSpend()` clamps to Math.Max(0, ...) (CardEnergyCost.cs:134-139), so the two agree on what is SPENT -- only what is READ diverges. Same mechanism and same verdict as card/ascenders_bane's and card/bad_luck's ctor entries (rule 3). DORMANT: the three ported cost readers agree today -- relics/mummified_hand.py:25 and potions.py:168 filter `> 0`, cards/event_cards.py:328 (Enlightenment) skips `<= 1` -- and events/infested_automaton.py:35 filters pool_card_ids(), which holds no curses. Live as soon as any effect reads an unplayable card's cost without a `> 0` filter.

OnPlay.rationale: CurseOfTheBell.cs declares no OnPlay and the card is Unplayable; the sim's abstract method is a `pass`.

guards.rationale: Inert for the same reason as card/ascenders_bane and card/clumsy: the flag only steers `DamageCmd.deal`'s prop inference and this card deals no damage.
